insight: tiller Session.run/1 is a blocking GenServer.call with the entire recursive loop inside handle_call/3 (session.ex), AND spawn_subagent calls Session.run/1 synchronously (actions.ex). Any async/observability work must change BOTH paths; inverting the session loop alone does not unblock the parent. Codex verified this against source after an initial 30-line estimate that was 3-5x low.

tiller is event-sourced not checkpointed: Tiller.State.log returns [{action,result}] and Tiller.FakeDriver.context takes a list of actions, so a recorded trajectory prefix is already a valid FakeDriver script and state-at-turn-N is Enum.take(log,n). No checkpointer needed. CAVEAT: replaying actions re-executes tools via Actions.eval, so deterministic replay requires injecting the recorded RESULT, not just replaying the action.

In this environment a compression hook lossily rewrites Bash stdout (drops words, collapses prose to telegraphic form). Reading structured content via `cat`/`sed` in Bash corrupts it — gstack skill section templates came back with placeholder blocks replaced by [->LNN] dedup pointers and unreadable prose. Use the Read tool for skill sections, templates, and any doc whose exact wording matters. A subagent reviewing a design doc hit the same class of problem with the Read summarizer and had to verify via sed/cat -A.

seed mcp serve wraps every port envelope as one text content item in the tools/call result; isError mirrors ok=false. Refusals carry error + exit (2 contention, 3 invalid transition, 4 not found, 6 fenced out); an unknown tool is a JSON-RPC -32602 error, not an envelope. task_get returns state at the top level and the card under "card", not under "task" (task is the id).

An open-seed instantiation on the fastcards backend (copy .seed/, set backend = "fastcards", git init + commit, seed init) is enough to drive the real engine with no remote and no credentials. Adding the test actor to [operators].actors lets it promote its own cards so claim paths are reachable.
